claim: Multi-component icosahedral shell stacking follows defined hexagonal lattice paths with seven chiral categories (MC, BG, Ch1-Ch5)
Optimal size mismatch ranges exist for each shell pair type: MC-MC (0.03-0.05), MC-Ch1 (0.12-0.16), MC-Ch2 (0.19-0.22), MC-BG (0.08-0.10)
MC shell configurations are energetically more favorable than Ch1 and BG configurations at each shell level
Theoretical size mismatch predictions agree with experimental measurements with R-squared = 0.9904
Dynamic growth simulations show convergence toward optimal mismatch values, with conservative path dominance (65%)
Lennard-Jones potentials govern inter-shell interactions with distinct equilibrium distances for each atomic pair
Predicted stable multi-shell clusters include Na13@Rb32, K13@Cs42, Ag13@Cu45 with specific size mismatch values
Two magic number sequences (Mackay b=3 and new b=5) define shell atom counts for icosahedral packing
Atomic pair compatibility is determined by size mismatch, enabling rational selection of element combinations
